subject: Runway sizing & deployment commitment — BlueHarbor private GPU pool
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Klein <sam.klein@blueharbor.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runway sizing & deployment commitment — BlueHarbor private GPU pool

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a short sizing worksheet and a proposed runway commitment that matches the latency/throughput targets you described. I attached the capacity_model_v2.xlsx and a simple network topology image (network_topology.png) for reference.

Top-line summary (so you can see decisions quickly):
- Target sustained throughput: 3.5k tokens/s for production AI features (peak bursts to ~9k tokens/s).
- Baseline pool: 8x A100-equivalent nodes (quantized model profile) + warm pool of 2 nodes for burst absorption.
- Expected tail latency P95: 160–220 ms for 512-token prompts under multiplexing configuration.
- Recommended commit: 6 months reserved with optional +2 node burst capability for first 30 days.

Action items / asks for you:
1) Confirm the expected 95th percentile latency target for critical endpoints (you said <250 ms; I assumed <220 ms in the worksheet).
2) Share any networking constraints (eg. egress limits, VPN termination window) that would affect headroom.
3) We can set up a short internal sizing review with your infra engineer — who should we loop in?

If helpful, Jonas and I can walk Priya through the capacity workbook tomorrow.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), network_topology.png (image)
From: Sam Klein <sam.klein@blueharbor.ai>

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway sizing & deployment commitment — BlueHarbor private GPU pool

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the files, looks useful. Quick clarifications before we schedule a deep dive: 

- The <250 ms target I mentioned was for our interactive feature (single-turn chat). The batch inference for analytics can tolerate up to 800 ms. So your assumption of <220 ms for interactive is OK (we prefer to leave some buffer).
- Networking: our VPC egress window is capped at 12 Gbps baseline; we can request temporary increases but lead time is 48 hours.
- Infra contact: Priya Rao (cc'ed) will own the VPN and network side; she may loop in one of our SREs for the port/security review.

Can you confirm the sizing assumptions for model quantization (INT8 vs 4-bit) used in the worksheet? We need to understand how node count changes if we go with more aggressive quantization. Also curious about your warm pool warm-up assumptions (how long to reach full KV cache efficiency).

Sam
CTO, BlueHarbor AI
sam.klein@blueharbor.ai | +1 617 555 0987

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Runway sizing & deployment commitment — BlueHarbor private GPU pool

Folks —

I reviewed Marissa's workbook overnight. A few internal notes I want us aligned on before we respond to Sam with specifics:

1) Quantization sensitivity: The current workbook assumes 4-bit quantization (LLM-int4 profile) for the 8-node baseline. If BlueHarbor opts for INT8, you'd need roughly +35% nodes to preserve throughput at same latency (so baseline becomes ~11 nodes). I flagged the formulas in the sheet (tab: quant_profiles).

2) Warm pool behavior: We model warm pool efficiency improvement as an exponential warmup — 60% effective at 60s, 90% effective at 5 minutes for KV-prefetch-friendly workloads. For very long tails / non-repeating prefixes you'll see slower gains. Include note in reply.

3) Network egress: 12 Gbps cap means your peak bursts will be gated — with our default batching and multiplexing we expect node-level egress of ~0.8 Gbps at peak for the proposed model. 8 nodes + 2 warm nodes pushes ~8x0.8 = 6.4 Gbps during a big burst (within the 12 Gbps cap), but additional services (metrics, backups) could add headroom usage. Recommend we list the egress assumptions explicitly.

4) Failure/fallback plan: If they want guaranteed sub-250 ms P95, recommend a safety margin of +1 reserved node or a regional fallback to hosted for peak spikes.

I'll draft a short reply that calls out: (a) INT8 vs 4-bit delta quantified, (b) warm pool warm-up numbers and recommended reserve, and (c) egress impact and mitigation. Marissa — want me to send directly to Sam/Priya or should I drop it to you for signature?

-Jonas
Principal Systems Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway sizing & deployment commitment — BlueHarbor private GPU pool

Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the quick clarifications and for looping Priya in. Per Jonas' notes below, two quick bullets to confirm and next steps: 

- Quantization: Workbook baseline uses 4-bit (LLM-int4). If you prefer INT8 for extra model fidelity, baseline ~= 11 nodes; if you stick with int4 we remain at 8 nodes. I've added both rows to the spreadsheet for clarity.
- Warm pool: expect ~60% cache effectiveness at 60s, ~90% by 5 minutes for common prefix workloads; plan assumes 2 warm nodes.
- Network: we modeled a peak egress of ~0.8 Gbps/node during bursts; 8+2 nodes sits comfortably under your 12 Gbps baseline but we'll note the assumptions and call out temporary throttle behavior.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can Priya share the SRE contact (name + email) so we can schedule a 45-minute network & sizing review?
2) If you want us to lock in a 6-month reserved commitment we can provide a formal term sheet once you confirm quantization preference.

I'll schedule a joint call for early next week once you share an SRE contact.

Best,

Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123
